claude.rationale: gap_45=1: the customer-facing product (Worldpay's global payments platform serving ~400,000 clients, T4) crossed the ownership boundary whole via the scheme of arrangement, but the filing frames the U.S. and global technology platforms/processing infrastructure (T5) as targets "to be harmonised" and integrated "going forward" rather than describing an already-unified processing substrate at closing — a documented product-vs-process mismatch. gap_56=0: the operational processes were not re-engineered at closing (integration was prospective), and the people/organization (T6) transferred coherently alongside — the board combined 8 Vantiv/5 Worldpay directors with a Co-CEO structure, and existing Worldpay management, employment and pension rights were confirmed and equity plans carried across. gap_mitigated=no: no transitional-services or shared-services agreement allocating a shared processing substrate is described in the reviewed filing sections. T1 coded imprint-share because both principals' intent is co-present — Vantiv remains the continuing Delaware registrant/filer while the combined entity adopts the Worldpay name with dual (Cincinnati/London) headquarters and a Co-CEO leadership.

gemini.rationale: The transaction was a whole-company acquisition of Worldpay Group plc by Vantiv, Inc. The entire business, including products (T4), processes (T5), and organization (T6), transferred together. There is no evidence of a structural mismatch or gap between products and processes, or processes and people, at closing.

openai.rationale: The transaction acquired Worldpay's entire share capital as a whole-company acquisition, so its customer-facing payments platform and the operations supporting it crossed the ownership boundary together; the statement that the two companies' infrastructures would be integrated and harmonised later does not document a product-process separation at closing. The combined board and executive structure included directors and Co-CEOs from both companies, while Worldpay employees' existing employment and pension rights were to be observed, so no closing-stage mismatch between transferred processes and the organization operating them is documented.
